## The Great Photography Exodus on /p/

The debate over the health of 4chan’s /p/ (Photography) board has reached a fever pitch, with users divided on whether the forum is dying or simply evolving. The central thesis from critics is that the board suffers from "funko-pop mental improvishment," where gear fetishism has overtaken artistic substance. A significant portion of the complaint focuses on the influx of repetitive spammers and "cargo-cultists" who idolize equipment over composition.

One notable thread highlighted a user named "cANON," who dominated a recent discussion with 27 out of 101 comments, suggesting that attention-seeking behavior is degrading the quality of discourse. Conversely, defenders argue that the harsh, exclusionary culture drives away contributors seeking constructive feedback, leaving only those eager for shallow validation. The consensus among the vocal minority is that basic rules of engagement are being ignored, allowing degenerates to set the tone. Meanwhile, in the /fgt/ Film General Thread, users are hashing out technical details, discussing the viability of Cinestill’s two-bath developer kit and debating the merits of slower film stocks for box cameras.

## Nostalgia Trips: 64-Bit Classics and SEGA Origins

On BlueSky, a wave of retro-gaming nostalgia is sweeping through the timeline, anchored by strong sentiments toward *Bomberman 64*. Users are hailing the title as an underrated highlight of the Nintendo 64 library, praising its multiplayer chaos and costume-collecting mechanics. One particularly touching anecdote shared a story of playing with their mother during her difficult transition to 3D gaming, underscoring the game’s accessibility. Contextual posts revealed the game’s turbulent development, noting that Hudson Soft scrapped over six months of work after seeing other 3D titles, eventually releasing it in Japan as *Baku Bomberman* in September 1997.

Simultaneously, @sonichedgeblog initiated a retrospective on BlueSky asking which SEGA console first introduced users to Sonic the Hedgehog. The thread has become a timeline of gaming history, with users reflecting on their initial exposure to the franchise via systems like the Master System or Genesis, serving as a communal look back at early Sonic gaming experiences.

## Wet Plate Chuds and Viral Lasagna Logic

The quirky vernacular of 4chan’s /gg/ (Gear General) board continues to thrive, with users jokingly rebranding the wet plate photography trend as "wet plate chud edition." The humor centers on a lens with humorous typos in its description ("squuizing b8"), touted for its ability to catch *surströmming* (fermented herring) on a hook. This serves as a cryptic, playful endorsement of the lens's extreme macro capabilities and short minimum focusing distance.

On BlueSky, logic-based observations are gaining traction. User @Bob Heller sparked a lighthearted debate by arguing that stacking one lasagna on top of another results in "one giant lasagna" rather than two distinct dishes, highlighting the unique structural properties of layered foods. Meanwhile, the "Yuri" genre is seeing a surge in engagement on Bsky, with aggregator @JAV Titles curating content that highlights a niche but enthusiastic audience segment actively celebrating the category.

## Quick Hits

*   **Sonic Box Art:** @Hourly Videogame Box Art shared a nostalgic look at the packaging for "Road 2," focusing purely on the aesthetic presentation for retro collectors.
*   **Spinal Health:** User Ed advocated for standing desks and proper lifting posture to avoid back pain by one’s thirties, contrasting his health at 38 with younger users who admit to poor habits. He ended a dramatic plea from @mothman the wanderer with the permissive advice: "go as thou wilt."
*   **Viral Reactions:** A cluster of posts featuring exaggerated "😱" emojis and the phrase "my expression fr" indicated a shared, humorous shock at a specific visual stimulus, though the source material remained unnamed.
*   **Unsuccessful Tries:** In 4chan’s /p/ Recent Photo Thread, users shared failed attempts at photographing aviation subjects, including a humorous confirmation to a user named Anon that their target plane had arrived.

context_texts: @4530530 - /p/ — Why is /p/ dead? — How come no one posts here? Photography is a pretty big hobby, and it has become very fashionable to shoot film in recent years, so why is this board completely abandoned?
clusters.summary: Users on 4chan’s /p/ board are debating why the photography forum appears abandoned, citing a lack of substantive engagement and an influx of repetitive spammers. Critics blame "funko-pop mental improvishment" and a culture of cargo-cultists who idolize gear over substance, noting that genuine posts are often dismissed by a majority focused on shallow validation. One user highlights that 27 of 101 comments in a recent thread belonged to a single user ("cANON"), arguing that such attention-seeking behavior degrades the board's quality. Conversely, supporters suggest that harsh criticism and the exclusion of non-establishment styles drive away contributors who seek constructive feedback rather than just praise. The consensus is that basic rules are being ignored, allowing degenerates to dictate the board's tone and discouraging effort.

Had an absolute blast collecting the costume pieces and playing multiplayer with friends and family.  I’m always surprised when I hear people being mixed on it. For me it’s a banger!

@Quest 64 Official  (quest64official.bsky.social) — Same My mom was/is a huge Bomberman fan so we got it pretty close to release  It was a hard transition for her moving to 3D, but she still enjoyed it and we played the hell out of the multiplayer

@Quest 64 Official  (quest64official.bsky.social) — September 26 1997, Bomberman 64 debuted as Baku Bomberman on the N64 in Japan!  Developer/Publisher Hudson Soft made the tough decision to scrap over 6 months of work on the initial version of the game and start fresh after seeing other 3D games/Atomic Bomberman PC already at market!
clusters.summary: Social media users are expressing strong nostalgia for *Bomberman 64*, specifically citing it as a highlight of the Nintendo 64 library. The topic centers on the game's legacy, with one user praising its multiplayer experience and costume-collecting mechanics as a "banger," while another shares a story of playing it with their mother despite her difficult transition to 3D gaming. Contextual details highlight the game's turbulent development, noting that Hudson Soft scrapped over six months of work after seeing other 3D titles and the *Atomic Bomberman* PC port, ultimately releasing it in Japan as *Baku Bomberman* on September 26, 1997. Overall, the sentiment is overwhelmingly positive, challenging the notion that the game receives mixed reviews.
